findings.summary: the new walk's `unwrap` was character-identical to `parameterIsReadOnly`'s and its `rootIdentifier` was a third copy of the chain unwind -- the property/element walk that has to unwrap BETWEEN steps; one module-level `unwrapExpression` and one exported `rootIdentifier` now serve all three, `Compiler.inferredObjectIsMutated` passing its own side-effecting unwrap

the three write shapes -- assignment, `++`/`--`, and a non-read-only method call on the root -- were spelled twice in one file, so `readOnlyDataMethods` had two independent consumers; `writesThroughRoot(node, isTarget)` takes the root predicate and both walks call it
`declaredWithin` reimplemented `ts.findAncestor`, which the pinned TypeScript exports and which also starts at the node itself; the 13-line function is gone

the `returnExpression` parameter was derivable at all three call sites, and `irFor` computed the same thing a second way; `finalReturnExpression` is now the one definition of what a function returns, and the parameter is dropped

the `!needsValueLambda &&` guard was dead -- that path omits `returnExpression` from the IR, so `lower()` never reads the flag -- and the recursive-group construction site set a value nothing reads; the guard is gone and the field is optional, omitted where recursive groups lower to real native functions

`writesOuterState` was named for half of what it held, reading false for a function that writes a captured binding and returns a local; renamed `returnNeedsSnapshot`, and its comment now carries the measurement that says why it rides the IR rather than being recomputed per call site (356 walks for 356 distinct declarations corpus-wide)

the expensive body walk ran unconditionally while the cheap return-expression check could veto it afterwards; measured at 21 of 57 walks skippable on doom and 63 of 94 on racer, so the read check runs first and the two halves are named `readsSharedBinding` and `writesSharedBinding`
`materializeScalar`'s number and boolean branches differed only in a type keyword; one `cppType` resolution emits both

`includeScalars` made one policy take a mode flag, so a caller chose which value shapes the escape policy covered -- and a bare escaping scalar not being materialized was the anomaly the flag patched; the two guarantees are two named methods now, `materializeEscapingValue` and `pinValueToTemporary`, and the caller picks the one it needs

`pinValueToTemporary` states the contract `enumMapLiteral`'s slot pinning already relied on -- a lowering that emits statements while producing a value binds that value, it does not splice it -- so the rule has one home and one vocabulary instead of two implementations under two names, and it records why its leaf stays separate from `materializeRecordScalars`'s

the four-member `SupportedFunction` union was narrowed by hand at two sites and the existing one had already drifted, omitting `isMethodDeclaration`; one `isSupportedFunction` guard makes that impossible

the `[[maybe_unused]]` platform-callback convention was hand-spelled at five sites and MISSING at the sixth -- `on_visibility_change`, the one site this branch did not otherwise touch; `compilePlatformCallback` now takes the parameter as `{cppType, name}` and renders it in one place, which repairs the divergent site (tetris is the one scene reaching it)
`returnedValueCanMove` was exported with no consumer outside its module, and `declaration.body!` needed a non-null assertion the guard had already made; both gone

docs/fidelity.md#physics-contract still read "Scene 40 carries one" while status.md had been updated to two rows, and the new registry entry cited that page as the authority for scene 100's ceiling; the page now names both and says why their ceilings are one measurement

the scene 100 row claimed to measure "that enabling collision events moves no pixel" while its gate is scene 40's solver band, inside which a perturbed simulation would pass; the registry comment and the status row now own what the gate owns -- the collision surface compiling and running at 40's pose against a golden byte-identical to 40's -- and the entry records why the golden is a separate file rather than a shared path (`--recapture-reference` writes through it, so sharing would let a scene 100 refresh overwrite scene 40's evidence)
